arguments.cause: I reproduced the Movement Units card on the Inventory Health page with no filters. Handled Quantity is SUM('Activity'[units]) and returns 8765. The Activity table holds 406 rows but only 360 distinct movement IDs. The model's Activity table is a Direct Lake read of the gold lakehouse table movement_values, and that table also sums to 8765, so the model adds nothing on top of the gold table. In movement_values, 46 movements appear on more than one row. Those 46 extra rows add 1104 units, which is exactly the gap between 8765 and the 7661 you calculated. Each of the 46 repeated movements has rows that differ in units or rate_version. If I keep one row per movement (taking the smallest units value), movement_values sums to 7661. That is my own regrouping of the gold table, not a read of ordersops. I could not query the ordersops source system: no query route to it could be opened, and movement_values has no recorded upstream dependency. So I have not confirmed in the source that it has 360 rows totalling 7661, and I cannot say at which step before movement_values the extra rows were introduced.

arguments.cause:
The extra 250 is invoice 101 (account 1, 250, 2026-10-01, ISSUED), which is counted twice. No other invoice is involved.

What I found:
- I re-ran Invoiced Amount, which is SUM(Billing[amount]), and got 950. The model's Billing table reads gold.invoice_activity, which also sums to 950.
- gold.invoice_activity has 5 rows: invoice 101 appears twice, once with plan 1 and once with plan 2. Invoices 102 (100), 103 (250) and 104 (100) appear once each.
- The bronze invoices table in billing_bronze has the same 4 invoices, one row each, and sums to 700. That matches your export total.
- The bronze account_plan_history table has two rows for account 1: plan 1 (valid 2026-09-01 to 2026-09-30) and plan 2 (valid from 2026-10-01 to 2099-12-31). Every other account has one row.

Likely cause: the retained definition of the gold.build_billing procedure builds gold.invoice_activity by LEFT JOINing silver.invoices to bronze.account_plan_history on account_id only. Nothing in that join limits it to the plan valid on the invoice date. An account with two plan-history rows therefore gets each of its invoices once per row, which matches the two copies of invoice 101 (250 x 2).

Limits:
- I couldn't read silver.invoices (the query was rejected), so I haven't confirmed it holds one row per invoice.
- The procedure definition is fixture-authoring code, and I have no proof it actually ran. Job runs were unavailable. The conclusion that the duplicate is created at the gold step relies on that definition plus the bronze and gold reads.
- I didn't query billingapp directly. Your 700 is matched only by the bronze table's total.
- Invoice 104 is VOID and is included in both the 700 and the 950.
